finding: Human audibility evidence is not sufficient unless it is bound to one exact commit, immutable deployment identifier, physical-device class, bounded session identifier, runtime route, and ordered fresh observation window.

primary.title: Web Audio API
primary.use: Defines AudioContext lifecycle, state, resume behavior, audio graph routing, and destination semantics.

primary.title: HTML Standard: User activation
primary.use: Defines transient and sticky user activation as browser-maintained state rather than a durable proof of later audible output.

evidence_strength: implementation-tested contract; physical-device behavior remains unobserved
observed: The canonical queue contains no active frontier_research item.
V-001 still requires bounded physical iPhone Safari audibility verification.
The prior audibility classifier distinguishes human-confirmed and contradicted evidence but does not bind the result to a deployment, session, and freshness window.
inferred: An unbound human report can be accidentally associated with the wrong build, deployment, device, or playback attempt.
proposed: Run the existing audibility classifier first, then validate the resulting terminal classification through this binding gate before accepting it into V-001 evidence.
superseded: Treating a human-confirmed classifier result alone as sufficient commit-bound deployment evidence.
unresolved: Physical iPhone Safari execution has not occurred.
Immutable Vercel deployment identity is not yet available for the blocked application commit.
Session identifiers still require a concrete generator and capture UI.
falsification_route: Reject this contract if a test demonstrates that accepted evidence can be replayed across deployments or device sessions.
Reject or revise the temporal bounds if real physical verification cannot complete within them without weakening deployment identity.
Treat any physical silent-output result as contradiction evidence, not success, even when the AudioContext reports running.
privacy_boundary: Retains only opaque commit, deployment, session, device-class, classification, boolean audibility, and timestamp fields; drops free-form notes and personal content.
